Arjun: FYI profiling showed a new p95 spike after the kernel-selector change this morning. repro on staging with AWQ+fp8 + kv-cache enabled.
Maya: ugh saw that in canary too, p95 jumped ~120ms on short prompts.
Liam: can you paste the profiler run? which flags?
Arjun: ran `./tools/run_profiler --model gpt-neo-12b-awq --seq 1024 --kernel auto --kv-dtype=int8`
Arjun: flamegraph attached (will paste gist) — big gap around kernel switch and small memcpy spikes during KV upcasts.
Nina: could be the dtype fallback path doing a temp upcast to fp16 for some layers then copying back for KV. we saw memcpy churn when workspace got fragmented.
Maya: config we used: `workspace.soft_reserve=512MB, deferred_free_ms=50, slab_min=32MB`
Liam: repro steps? I can try with workspace.soft_reserve=768MB and slab_min=64MB to reduce fragmentation.
Arjun: repro steps: 1) warm KV with 4x prefix 2) send 8 concurrent short-stream requests 3) observe p95. I have a short command:```
scripts/load_kv_prefix.sh --model gpt-neo-12b-awq --prefix-size 4
ab -n 200 -c 8 -p payload.json http://staging:8080/generate
```
Maya: quick numbers from my run: baseline p95=180ms, after kernel-selector change p95=300ms, memory allocs spikes correlating at ~2.1GB extra transient.
Nina: hypothesis: kernel-selector picks a faster kernel that requires an intermediate fp16 scratch buffer for quantized kernels; allocator tries to scatter small frees -> fragmentation -> memcpy-based consolidation -> latency spike.
Liam: mitigation ideas: 1) prefer kernel variant with no intermediate scratch for latency-critical routes, 2) coalesce small frees by extending deferred_free_ms, 3) pre-reserve a compact snapshot region from the pool for KV upcasts.
Arjun: I prototyped a "snapshot" prefetch: before generation we allocate a small contiguous buffer, touch it so it's resident, then route KV upcast into it. dropped p95 by ~60ms locally.
Maya: oh nice. can you share the snippet?
Arjun: snippet:```c
// prefetch compact snapshot
void *snap = allocator.alloc_contiguous(RESERVED_SNAPSHOT_BYTES);
memset(snap, 0, RESERVED_SNAPSHOT_BYTES); // fault pages in
kv_upcast_into(snap);
// generate
allocator.free_delayed(snap, /*delay_ms=*/150);
```
Nina: that delayed-free trick buys time so the allocator doesn't fragment and we avoid memcpy compaction under load.
Liam: can we generalize: workspace.snapshot_size per-model + route hint to kernel-selector to avoid fp16-scratch variants when snapshot enabled?
Maya: sounds good. also we should add a fallback to force KV cache dtype=float16 if int8 path causes too many copies. tradeoff is raw memory vs copy cost.
Arjun: agreed. plan: 1) add `workspace.snapshot_size` config knob and `route.kernel_preference` override; 2) run A/B on canary and measure p50/p95/mem transient; 3) implement allocator hint to prefer compact contiguous allocs for KV upcasts.
infra-bot: deployed canary image `inference/runtime:staging-kernel-171850` to cluster staging-2 (rollout 12%).
Maya: I'll run synthetic load against staging-2 and post results in 30m. @Arjun @Liam please pair on the allocator hint change (Nina can review). :thumbsup:
Liam: ack, will start a branch and ping for review.
Arjun: thanks — if this gets us back to baseline we can keep kernel-selector perf-opt but with the snapshot fallback for latency routes.
Maya: ETA for a patch and canary metric in PR? 4 hours?
Liam: aim for PR in 3h, canary in 4.
Nina: added a checklist: [x] repro script, [ ] allocator hint, [ ] route overrides, [ ] canary metrics dashboard.
Maya: perfect.
Arjun: adding logs to the p95 dashboard for transient allocs and memcpy counts so we can quantify.
infra-bot: alert suppressed for transient-mem-surge on staging-2 while tests run.
